title: Why Use MiniJinja from DuckDB?
description: Render [MiniJinja](https://github.com/mitsuhiko/minijinja) templates inside SQL with a JSON context. MiniJinja is Armin Ronacher's Rust port of [Jinja2](https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/) — strict Python-Jinja2 semantics in a small, fast core. This extension exposes it as a scalar function, so each query row can produce its own rendered string — emails, config blocks, dynamic SQL, webhook payloads — without leaving DuckDB.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: Anywhere you'd otherwise pull rows out of DuckDB to feed into a Jinja loop in Python, `minijinja_render` collapses that loop into a single SQL projection. The template stays declarative; the data stays in the query.

bulletPoints.label: Per-row HTML / email
bulletPoints.description: Build the body of a transactional email per row: pass the row's columns as a JSON object via [`json_object`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/functions/json) and render against a template literal.

bulletPoints.label: Config-file generation
bulletPoints.description: Materialize one nginx / systemd / Kubernetes manifest per row of a configuration table. Disable autoescape with `autoescape := false` for non-HTML output.

bulletPoints.label: Dynamic SQL
bulletPoints.description: Use MiniJinja as a meta-SQL preprocessor — render `SELECT ... FROM {{ table }} WHERE {{ pred }}` against context columns, then execute the result. Treat templates as **trusted**; Jinja interpolation is not parameter-safe.

bulletPoints.label: Notifications and webhook payloads
bulletPoints.description: Render Slack / PagerDuty / generic webhook JSON bodies straight from query results so a single SQL pipeline takes you from event to delivered message.

sections.title: How it works
sections.description: A scalar function backed by the [`minijinja`](https://docs.rs/minijinja/) Rust crate. Each call compiles the template, binds the JSON context, and returns the rendered text. There is no `ATTACH`, no secrets, no template registry — one function name and a couple of optional named arguments.

bulletPoints.label: Template + context
bulletPoints.description: First argument is the template (a `VARCHAR` literal or column). Second argument, when present, is a DuckDB `JSON` value — a literal string, [`json_object(...)`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/functions/json), or a column. Templates without variables work without any context at all.

bulletPoints.label: Strict Jinja2 semantics
bulletPoints.description: MiniJinja deliberately tracks Python-Jinja2 behavior — undefined-variable handling, filter naming, scoping, autoescape rules. If a template renders correctly under Python's [Jinja2](https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/) for these basic features, it should render the same here.

bulletPoints.label: Standard vocabulary
bulletPoints.description: Filters (`upper`, `lower`, `length`, `default`, `join`, `replace`, etc.), control flow (`if` / `elif` / `else`, `for` with `loop.index` / `loop.first` / `loop.last`), tests (`is defined`, `is none`), and string concatenation. See the [MiniJinja crate docs](https://docs.rs/minijinja/) for the full surface.

bulletPoints.label: Autoescape on by default
bulletPoints.description: HTML special characters in context values are escaped — safe default for HTML / email output. Pass `autoescape := false` when generating raw text (configs, SQL, JSON payloads).

sections.title: MiniJinja vs Tera
sections.description: This catalog ships two Jinja-style template engines as DuckDB extensions: MiniJinja and [`tera`](/products/extensions/tera). They overlap heavily — both render `{{ var }}` / `{% for %}` / `{% if %}` against JSON context. The differences are real but narrow.

bulletPoints.label: Pick MiniJinja for Jinja2 fidelity
bulletPoints.description: MiniJinja deliberately tracks [Python Jinja2](https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/) semantics — naming, scoping, filter behavior. Choose it when you have an existing Python-Jinja codebase and want your DuckDB templates to behave the same way, or when you're already fluent in Jinja2.

bulletPoints.label: Pick Tera for the larger feature surface
bulletPoints.description: [`tera`](/products/extensions/tera) ships a wider [built-in filter and tester library](https://keats.github.io/tera/docs/#built-ins), template inheritance via a `template_path` glob, and Tera-specific extensions to the Jinja syntax. Choose it when your templates lean on those features or when you already maintain a Tera template library.

bulletPoints.label: Either is fine for everyday substitution
bulletPoints.description: For `{{ name }}` / `{{ x | upper }}` / `{% for x in xs %}`, both produce identical output. Lock in whichever syntax matches your team's existing templates.

useCases.title: Render transactional emails per row
useCases.description: One row per recipient, one `minijinja_render` call producing the HTML body — fed straight into a downstream sender.

useCases.title: Generate per-host configuration
useCases.description: A `virtual_hosts` table plus a single MiniJinja template equals one rendered nginx / Caddy / Envoy block per host, ready to write to disk or push to a config repo.

useCases.title: Build dynamic SQL from metadata
useCases.description: Drive `SELECT` / `CREATE TABLE` shape from a metadata table — MiniJinja renders the SQL, your driver executes it. Useful for codegen, schema migrations, and templated reporting.

useCases.title: Format Slack / webhook payloads
useCases.description: Render alert JSON bodies directly from the query that detected the alert. Pair with [`http_client`](/products/extensions/http_client) to deliver them in the same pipeline.
